metadata.name: Steady 120
metadata.author: Pedaleira
metadata.summary: A solid-state clean amp with no distortion of its own: two transistor gain stages around the volume pot, a treble, middle and bass tone stack and a solid-state power amp with feedback that is linear up to its rails and clips flat there. The framework's stages are tube stages; here they stand for transistor stages and are given bias and cutoff voltages (30 V and 60 V) far above any signal they see, so they never bend, and the supply does not sag. A typical topology of the kind, not the schematic of one product; its values were fitted to measurements of a reference amp (its VOLUME sweep, its response with every knob at 5 and its tone knob sweeps). Every value the fit moved is marked "fitted" with what it was fitted to.
references: D. T. Yeh and J. O. Smith, the closed-form analysis of the treble, middle and bass tone stack, DAFx-06, 2006
J. Pakarinen and D. T. Yeh, A review of digital techniques for modeling vacuum-tube guitar amplifiers, Computer Music Journal 33(2), 2009

Pedaleira measurements of a reference amp played through a modelling unit's USB input: GAIN sweeps with a 1 kHz staircase, THD at the staircase's -18 dBFS step, the test signal's sweeps and the tone knob sweeps (2026), with the signal 24 dB under its nominal level
